previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and a history of recurrent atrial tachycardia was admitted after developing palpitations with a heart rate of 120–130 during dialysis, following fluid removal and withholding of metoprolol. She was hypotensive initially but responded to fluid resuscitation. Workup showed no myocardial infarction, with stable troponins and no growth on blood cultures. An echocardiogram revealed diastolic dysfunction and moderate pulmonary hypertension without significant change from prior. The electrophysiology team recommended transitioning from diltiazem and metoprolol to amiodarone to avoid hypotension and better control arrhythmias. Warfarin was adjusted to 1 mg daily due to interaction with amiodarone. She remained stable, completed a hemodialysis session, and was discharged to extended care with updated medications and close follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with past medical history of 
atrial tachycardia, end stage renal failure on hemodialysis, 
diastolic congestive heart failure and type 2 insulin dependent 
diabetes mellitus admitted for new onset left-sided chest pain.  

.  
#1. Chest pain: Given reproducibility of pain on exam with 
palpation and improvement on pain medications, her chest pain 
was deemed to be musculoskeletal in origin. CXR showed pulmonary 
edema but no evidence of infection. BNP elevated at >3000. EKG 
was without new ischemic changes, trops negative x 4: (0.03--> 
0.05 -->0.07-->0.07 in setting of ESRD).  No events on telemetry 
over 48 hours of monitoring; her chest pain was therefore 
considered to unlikely be cardiac in origin.  
- Pain control was provided with tylenol and dilaudid during 
admission; the patient was requiring only Tylenol at the time of 
discharge. Her chest pain improved over the course of this 
hospitalization. She is now discharged on Tylenol prn for her 
chest pain.
.
#2. Leukocytosis: Ms. ___ was noted to have an elevated WBC of 
10.3 on admission.  This was noted to trend down without 
antibiotic intervention by hospital day #1. It was thought to be 
due to inguinal skin boils that she had experienced in the days 
prior to admission that were noted to be resolving. She remained 
afebrile throughout this hospitalization. Her WBC at the time of 
discharge was normal at 7.0.
.  
#3. Acute on chronic diastolic congestive heart failure: Ms. 
___ was noted to be more hypervolemic for the several days 
prior to admission in the setting of dietary indiscretion.  
- She had hemodialysis according to her ___ 
schedule on HD#1 for more aggressive fluid removal and was kept 
on a low salt diet.
- She was encouraged to continue a low salt, diabetic diet at 
___. 
.  
#4. End stage renal disease: 
- As mentioned above, she received hemodialysis and her 
sevelamer and Epogen were continued per her outpatient regimen.
.  
#5. Diabetes Mellitus type 2: She was kept on her home regimen 
of 20 units NPH insulin QAM and also placed on an insulin 
sliding scale.
.  
#6. History of deep venous thrombosis: The patient was noted to 
have a supratherapeutic INR of 4.3 on admission. As a result, 
her coumadin was held during this hospitalization. At the time 
of discharge, her INR was noted to be 4.1.  She should have an 
INR checked at minimum every other day upon discharge, and her 
coumadin should be restarted when her INR is approximately 2.5.  
In addition, she will require at least weekly outpatient 
monitoring of her INR to ensure a therapeutic goal of 2.0-3.0.
.  
#7. Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Ms. ___ was ordered for CPAP 
during this admission.   
.  
# Atrial tachycardia: She was noted to be in sinus rhythm 
throughout hospitalization. She was continued on her outpatient 
regimen of amiodarone.    
.  
#8. Depression: Continued on paroxetine.  
.  
#9. History of MRSA/current inguinal boils: Did not appear 
infected, these were monitored closely and treated with topical 
antibiotic ointment and daily dressing changes. She was also 
continued on her outpatient regimen of MRSA prophylaxis with 
Bactrim since she has had coagulase positive staph bacteremia in 
the past and has a left subclavian line in place for 
hemodialysis purposes.  
.  
Ms. ___ code status was confirmed as FULL CODE during this 
admission. She was deemed medically stable and fit for discharge 
to ___ on ___. She will have follow-up with her 
primary care appointment within two weeks of discharge.  She 
will continue with her outpatient schedule for hemodialysis, 
with her next hemodialysis session scheduled for ___.
